LLM_description_template:
To: Supply Chain Leadership Team  
From: Sustainability & Logistics Director  
Subject: Balanced Shipping Plan — Cost, CO2, and Operating Rules  
Date: [Insert Date]

Context
Our distribution network moves product from multiple warehouses to our stores through lanes that carry both a dollar cost per unit and a CO2 emission rate per unit. In practice, the lowest-cost lanes often have the highest emissions. Balancing budget performance with our sustainability commitments requires a shipping plan that evaluates both metrics together while respecting day-to-day operating realities at docks and on the road.

Operational Rules
- Route setup/activation costs: Placing any lane into service triggers a one-time setup charge (e.g., carrier contracts, paperwork, dock preparations). A lane is either used or not; if used, the setup cost is incurred regardless of shipment volume.  
- Minimum order quantities: If we activate a lane, we must move at least the lane’s minimum volume to justify equipment, driver time, and loading efficiency. Partial loads below this threshold are not accepted.  
- Supplier limits per store: Each store can receive deliveries from no more than a policy-defined number of warehouses. This cap reflects receiving dock capacity, vendor management complexity, and contract terms.

Supply and Demand Realities
- Warehouses have finite inventory available for shipment; we cannot allocate more than what each facility can release.  
- Stores have required demand that must be met to protect on-shelf availability and service levels. Shortfalls are not acceptable.

Management Priority
Leadership has set relative importance weights for cost and emissions. We will evaluate each feasible shipping plan by combining:
- Weighted total variable transportation cost,
- Weighted total emissions, and
- The full value of route setup costs for any activated lanes.
Only the per-unit variable costs and emissions are weighted; setup charges are added in full.

Business Goal
Identify which lanes to activate and how much to ship on each active lane so that:
- Warehouse inventory is not exceeded,  
- Each store’s demand is fully covered,  
- Any activated lane ships at least its minimum order quantity,  
- Each store receives from no more than the allowed number of warehouses, and  
- The combined total of weighted variable cost, weighted emissions, and setup costs is as low as possible.
The resulting plan will show the trade-offs clearly, enabling leadership to confirm the balance between budget discipline and emissions reduction while staying within operational constraints.

ANNEX — Data Template
- Number of warehouses (sources): {NUM_SOURCES}
- Number of stores (destinations): {NUM_DESTINATIONS}
- Warehouse supplies (units available at each source): {SUPPLIES}
- Store demands (units required at each destination): {DEMANDS}
- Per-unit shipping cost matrix ($/unit by source–destination): {COST_MATRIX}
- Per-unit emission rate matrix (kg CO2/unit by source–destination): {EMISSION_MATRIX}
- Cost weight (importance assigned to variable cost): {WEIGHT_COST}
- Emission weight (importance assigned to emissions): {WEIGHT_EMISSION}
- Route setup/activation costs ($ per source–destination): {FIXED_COSTS}
- Minimum order quantities per route (units): {MIN_ORDER_QUANTITIES}
- Maximum number of suppliers allowed per store: {MAX_SUPPLIERS_PER_STORE}
